item.title: Autumn wreaths and 'doorscaping': Why we need more life in our front gardens
item.description: There was a time when decorative wreaths appeared on front doors in December, stayed on front doors for a few weeks and then disappeared. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Diamond laser system achieves 100% optical contrast in magnetic-field readout
item.description: Researchers at Fraunhofer IAF have developed a laser-enhanced quantum sensor that combines high magnetic-field sensitivity with a large dynamic range. Using laser threshold magnetometry, they improved the ratio of sensitivity and dynamic range by a factor of up to 590 compared with state-of-the-art approaches. The breakthrough is enabled by the first demonstration of 100% optical contrast, combined with strong laser readout signals. The results, published in Nature Communications, open up new prospects for medical diagnostics, navigation, and resource exploration. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Entrepreneurs live longer than salaried workers, study reveals
item.description: Conventional wisdom suggests that the long hours and pressures of entrepreneurship can take a toll on health. But new research by Cristiano Bellavitis, associate professor in the School of Business at Stevens Institute of Technology, and his collaborators finds that entrepreneurs tend to live longer than people who spend their careers working for others. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Quantum interference traps electron waves in metal for first time
item.description: Ever since quantum mechanics first described particles, like electrons, as rippling waves, researchers have wondered if those waves could be trapped in place. Writing today in Science a century later, a team of Columbia University researchers reports waves of electrons becoming trapped for the first time in a metal called Pd₅AlI₂. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Global warming may have halted an emerging ice age, study suggests
item.description: Two thousand years ago, the Arctic remnants of a once-vast ice sheet started to grow again. It was the beginning of a new glacial period, more conversationally known as the next ice age—but by the 1960s, summer temperatures were already so high that the ice sheet started to shrink. In other words, global warming ended a period of glaciation that had already begun. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Earth's hemispheres may have worked together to drive past ice ages
item.description: New research from the University of St Andrews has uncovered a previously unknown process that may have helped drive Earth into past ice ages. Published today (Oct. 22) in the Journal of Climate, the paper links ice sheets in the Northern Hemisphere to changes in ocean circulation and sea ice in the Southern Hemisphere understood to drive down atmospheric CO₂. Linking these two key features of the ice ages has long been a challenge, given how far apart the two regions are. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Webb captures stars in the early stages of life in a nearby stellar nursery
item.description: The NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope continues to reveal hidden parts of the cosmos with its advanced suite of infrared instruments. In a newly released image, Webb revealed many stars previously hidden by the dust clouds of NGC 7129, a stellar nursery about 3,300 light-years from Earth in the constellation Cepheus. The image is already improving our understanding of how new stars are born and evolve with time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Webb image reveals young stars brewing in a nebulous cauldron
item.description: In this Picture of the Month from the NASA/ESA James Webb Space Telescope, we visit a turbulent cauldron of star formation to see what is brewing inside dense clumps of gas. This is a star-forming region named LHA 120-N 159, or simply N159, located 161,000 light-years away in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), one of the satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way galaxy. This image spans about 230 light-years across. Publicado también por: European Space Agency. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists turn art detectives to date van Gogh's 'Starry Night' to actual sky from 1889
item.description: A team of South Korean researchers has put forward a new date for the night sky depicted in Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh's famed masterpiece "The Starry Night". Art historians have long assumed the stars were a product of the artist's fantasy or dated the scene to June 1889 based on the artist's location and other details, but astronomical details like the sliver crescent moon don't line up. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Mosquito bites are more complicated than they appear—getting a closer look might lead to better disease prevention
item.description: Female mosquitoes need blood to produce eggs. While much research has focused on how these hungry mosquitoes find their targets, less is known about what happens after they land on skin. Yet, a better understanding may allow researchers to find new ways of preventing bites that transmit diseases like malaria and dengue. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: When climate data is transformed into visuals, some people and places get overlooked
item.description: When a climate disaster happens, people thousands of miles away may encounter it through numbers: how many people died, how many were displaced, how many homes were destroyed and how much infrastructure was damaged. But for the people living through it, the disaster is not a data set. It is a home, a family, a livelihood and a place. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hay una buena razón por la que Elon Musk quiere juntar Tesla y SpaceX en una empresa de 3,5 billones de dólares: mas control
item.description: El martes, durante la conferencia de resultados de SpaceX , Elon Musk confirmaba que ambas empresas han formado comités especiales para estudiar una fusión. Esta idea de unir SpaceX y Tesla lleva un tiempo pululando y tras la unión entre la firma espacial de Musk y xAI , es un paso que al magnate le interesa especialmente. La empresa combinada tendría un valor de unos 3,5 billones de dólares a los valores actuales de mercado, según cuenta el New York Times, y sería la mayor operación corporativa de la historia en términos económicos. De momento no se ha acordado nada, pero el tema está desde… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Vallejo

item.title: Drought shifts more plant root cells into newly discovered environmental response mode
item.description: Scientists have discovered a hidden layer of identity in plant root cells: an "environmental mode" that switches on in some cells and becomes more common when water is scarce. The study, led by Dr. Marina Oliva and professor Ryan Lister, from the ARC Center of Excellence in Plants for Space and The University of Western Australia's School of Molecular Sciences, examined how plant cells responded to drought conditions. The work is published in Nature Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How does fake tan work, and why does it sometimes smell 'cookie-like'?
item.description: Real tans come from UV-triggered pigment production in living skin; that same UV exposure increases the risk of skin cancer. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: This group may be small, but McNeil River Falls is home to one of the largest seasonal congregations of bears on Earth, with as many as 80 being spotted at once
item.description: This group may be small, but McNeil River Falls is home to one of the largest seasonal congregations of bears on Earth, with as many as 80 being spotted at once Great picture Ver más comentarios Naveen Chilakapati Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: NASA’s Hubble Charts Path for Roman with Gravitational Lenses
item.description: This observation is one of many gravitational lensing images taken by Hubble in preparation for science with the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Are you using AI to study? Here's how to do it well
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) means high school and college students now have access to a resource that can potentially "do all the work for them." While this can reduce students' immediate stress about submitting assignments, it may negatively impact their long-term learning. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Supermassive black holes ejected from galactic centers? Quasar survey supports decade-old prediction
item.description: By analyzing data on around 100,000 quasars, or extremely luminous galactic nuclei, researchers at Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) have found statistical evidence that some supermassive black holes at the centers of galaxies are ejected from their positions after forming. The relationship now identified in the data was predicted 10 years ago by members of the same research group, Peter Raffai and Zsolt Frei, together with Zoltán Haiman. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The same novel can spark very different inner worlds in readers
item.description: Every storybook opens a window for our imagination to be freed from the reality of the world around us and escape into the fictional world. While the author's words act as a guide, everyone experiences fiction in their own way, creating vivid mental pictures and even forming an emotional connection with the characters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tire-derived pollutant found at elevated levels in critical fish habitats
item.description: Endangered coho salmon and steelhead trout live and spawn in habitats surrounded by human activity, such as the San Francisco Bay Area. During a recent storm, researchers found high levels of the tire-derived pollutant 6PPD-quinone in roadway outflows, creeks and rivers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A SpaceX no le gusta que China le pise los talones, así que va a hacer lo que nadie ha hecho: recuperar y reutilizar las dos etapas de un cohete
item.description: Parece que a Elon Musk no le gusta sentir que alguien le pisa los talones. Hace tiempo que la compañía china Deep Blue Aerospace publicó su interés en recuperar un cohete mediante un sistema de torre con palillos, como Mechazilla. Ahora, además, ha anunciado que las primeras piezas del cohete están saliendo de la cadena de montaje y que todo va viento en popa. Ha sido el momento ideal para que SpaceX anuncie que intentará algo aún más difícil que lo que ya hizo en Mechazilla: recuperar las dos etapas de su cohete Starship mediante ese sistema. Hasta ahora, ni SpaceX ni ninguna otra compañía… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Research tackling immature fruit drop in avocado trees
item.description: Only a percentage of avocados ever make it to harvest, but CSIRO research is working on ways to combat what is called immature fruit abscission or early fruit drop, a major challenge faced by growers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: World-first basic income trial boosts Indigenous livelihoods and Amazon rainforest protection
item.description: A pilot project in which Indigenous people in the Peruvian Amazon were given an unconditional basic income significantly improved community well-being, strengthened food security and supported rainforest protection, according to analysis by the University of Bath released today. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How much control do we have over picking up an accent? A lot, study finds
item.description: Have you ever binge-watched Bluey or a British crime drama and caught yourself imitating the characters' accents out loud? Rest assured, you are not alone. While it's a common belief that picking up someone else's accent just happens automatically, new research from The Ohio State University suggests that people actually have considerable control over when they adopt or suppress someone else's accent. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Black hole observations uncover evidence of solar storm–like magnetic eruptions
item.description: Technion researchers have presented evidence for the existence of solar-storm-like outbursts near supermassive black holes, which can be a million times larger than the sun or more. The phenomenon was discovered in the vicinity of the black hole in the galaxy NGC 3783, and the researchers' findings were published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fear of giving too little can stop people from giving at all
item.description: We've all done it: convinced ourselves that if we can't donate enough money to a cause, it's better not to give at all. But new research led by Jean Zhang, now a postdoctoral researcher at the Wharton School, suggests we're setting the bar for generosity far too high. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Gut bacteria use food cues to help time nutrient absorption, study finds
item.description: Biological clocks are often associated with light. Historically, most people started their days when the sun was up and ended their days when the sun set. But new research from Carnegie Mellon University suggests that some of the body's most important timekeepers live in the gut. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New study traces van Gogh's famed 'Starry Night' to an actual night sky from 1889
item.description: Scientists doubling as art detectives have traced Vincent van Gogh's "The Starry Night" to a celestial scene that suggests a new date for one of the world's most famous paintings. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: There should be black holes in our neighborhood. Can we find them?
item.description: Scientific estimates show that there should be between about 100 million and 1 billion stellar-mass black holes in the Milky Way. But they aren't easy to locate. They're not like supermassive black holes (SMBH) at the centers of galaxies. Those are usually easy to spot for different reasons. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Curtain-like plasma structures explain solar jets' apparent spinning in simulations
item.description: An international team of scientists from the University of Sheffield and the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, led by a postdoctoral research fellow from the University of Newcastle, Australia, has discovered that solar jets called spicules, which are 6–8 Mm long, take the form of warped, denser plasma sheets like pleated drapery. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Drone measurements reveal rapid early growth in eastern Australian humpback whales
item.description: Eastern Australian humpback whales reach nearly their full adult size quickly, a new Griffith University–led study has found, as shown by the first contemporary growth curves for this recovering whale population. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Young women can improve their online experience without giving up social media
item.description: Young women are often exposed to social media content that can contribute to negative body image, but new research has found small, deliberate changes to their feeds could help reduce body image pressures. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 350th ESA Council: Media information session
item.description: Video: 01:45:34 Watch the replay of the media information session where ESA Director General Josef Aschbacher and ESA Council Chair at delegate level Juan Carlos Cortés outline the key decisions and main outcomes of the 350th Council meeting held at ESA Headquarters in Paris on 21—22 October 2026. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: En 2023, veinte camiones cruzaron Países Bajos cargados con 400 toneladas de marisma frisia. Su destino era un canal capaz de fabricar tormentas
item.description: Es septiembre de 2023 y estamos en una reserva natural en la costa de Frisia. Hay varias excavadoras clavando en el suelo moldes de acero de dos metros por dos metros. Es, salvando las distancias, lo que Pim Willemsen, investigador de Wageningen y Deltares , llamaba un "cortador de galletas gigante" . El único problema es que cada galleta pesaba entre tres y seis toneladas . Esta es la historia de cómo unos investigadores neerlandeses trasladaron 66 de esas "galletas" en unos 20 camiones y las llevaron hasta Delft para meterlas en un canal de olas. ¿El motivo? Demostrar que esa marisma frisia… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Javier Jiménez

item.title: Legal encounters may offer overlooked opportunities for suicide prevention, analysis suggests
item.description: Picture a forlorn man walking into a lawyer's office after his marriage has collapsed. The bank is threatening foreclosure, and his finances are in tatters. His problems may be legal on paper, but in person they can look far more complicated: panic, shame or the numb resignation of someone who can no longer imagine a way out. He did not come for counseling, and his lawyer is not a therapist. Still, the attorney may be sitting beside him at the worst moment of his life—with a chance to help before despair slides into tragedy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Raised brows and a slow blink make speakers look more confident
item.description: Researchers studying facial movements have found that it's not just what you say, but what your face does when you say it, that counts when it comes to appearing confident when answering a question. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Amid cost‑of‑living worries and concern for the nation's future, stress is reshaping Americans' lives
item.description: U.S. adults appear increasingly likely to view stress as an unavoidable part of daily life, according to the 2026 Stress in America survey by the American Psychological Association. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Schrödinger's penguin: One species, two contrasting outcomes
item.description: A new University of Otago—Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka study reveals two vastly different life courses for one of Aotearoa New Zealand's least-studied penguin species. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Implicit language hierarchies in English-taught programs create ambivalent positions for multilingual students
item.description: A new study by Miki Shibata, a professor at Hiroshima University's Graduate School of Humanities and Social Sciences, reveals a paradox in Japan's English-medium higher education: Official English instruction coexists with local peer expectations that drive classroom interactions back into Japanese. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study finds NYC tenant right-to-counsel program linked to fewer ED visits in high-risk neighborhoods
item.description: Residential evictions are associated with adverse health outcomes, particularly among low-income populations. Less is known, however, about whether interventions designed to prevent evictions can improve health outcomes—including whether they may reduce visits to the emergency department (ED). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Lost Schrödinger manuscript reveals his true view of quantum randomness
item.description: Unlike classical physics, quantum mechanics generally cannot tell us exactly what will happen in an individual event. Instead, it predicts the probabilities of different outcomes. As one of the theory's early pioneers, Erwin Schrödinger played a key role in debates about what this randomness really means. However, part of his contribution has stayed hidden for more than 80 years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Some fish might thrive in a warming climate
item.description: Adelaide University researchers have found that some estuarine fishes that live in habitats with highly variable temperatures can withstand the warmer ocean conditions expected to result from climate change. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tokyo's streets reveal hidden gaps in urban inclusion and quality
item.description: Citywide measures of urban sustainability can conceal sharp differences between neighborhoods. A city may appear to provide good streets overall while some areas lack greenery, openness or pedestrian-friendly space where diverse populations live. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Christina Koch, astronauta del Artemis, a días de recibir el Premio Princesa de Asturias: “Espero que aprendamos que es importante conservar y amar el planeta en que nos encontramos”
item.description: Lo dijo la nueva subdirectora de la NASA, en el marco de una conferencia de prensa en Oviedo, donde recibirá la distinción este viernes; se trata de la única mujer que participó de la histórica misión a la Luna Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Birds are more afraid of women than men. Scientists have no idea why
item.description: Scientists have uncovered a strange pattern in urban bird behavior: Across five European countries and 37 species, birds consistently fled sooner when approached by women than men. Researchers have no clear explanation for the difference, raising intriguing questions about how birds recognize and respond to humans. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Family legacy helps explain how heirs decide to donate inherited possessions
item.description: There's a good reason why that fine china set or crystal stemware collection inherited from grandma sits in a box gathering dust in the basement. According to new research co-written by a University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign marketing expert, consumers don't simply donate family heirlooms and move on from them when they no longer spark joy. Instead, they remain concerned with how those heritage goods will be passed on to new owners and whether their legacy will continue. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Paying for the past: Norway's finder's fees favor gold's weight over what it tells us
item.description: Ten years ago, in 2016, a metal detectorist came upon a hoard of gold. It had been buried in the dirt for around 1,800 years and consisted of around 396 grams (14 ounces) of gold rings. The detectorist handed in his finds to a museum and received the largest finder's fee ever paid out in Norwegian history. He had been rewarded for the gold weight, not its rarity. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Q&A: What's innovative about canned food?
item.description: To most consumers, canned food is an everyday convenience, but to John Coupland, professor of food science at Penn State, each can represents more than two centuries of invention, experimentation and problem-solving. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A revolutionary new microscope could reveal the hidden machinery of life
item.description: Researchers have developed a revolutionary microscope that uses an incredibly powerful laser to make previously invisible cellular structures easier to see. The technology dramatically improves image clarity, allowing scientists to examine small proteins that conventional electron microscopes struggle to capture. It could eventually reveal how tiny molecular machines interact inside cells, providing an unprecedented look at the hidden workings of life. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Parental benefit encouraged people to have children in Estonia, but fathers mainly applied for financial reasons
item.description: A generous parental leave reform was introduced in Estonia in 2004. This increased the likelihood of a second or third child being born into the family and also shortened the interval between births, according to Sanan Abdullayev's doctoral thesis, defended at Tallinn University. At the same time, taking shared parental leave did not necessarily mean that the father took time off work and assumed primary responsibility for the children while receiving the benefit. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s Curiosity rover reveals a spectacular new view of Mars with a mystery on the horizon
item.description: NASA’s Curiosity rover has revealed a spectacular new view of mysterious, wind-carved cliffs on Mars that may hold evidence of ancient volcanic activity. With the rover approaching these unusual formations, scientists hope to uncover the secrets behind their strange appearance in 2027. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover dangerous water oscillations between Lake Varna and Black Sea
item.description: For years, pilots have observed strong and unusual currents in the 2.4-kilometer-long (1.5-mile-long), 300-meter-wide (984-foot-wide) canal connecting Lake Varna with the Black Sea. Maarja Kruusmaa, an academician and professor at Tallinn University of Technology, and researcher Laura Piho, working with the Port of Varna, undertook detailed measurements to determine the causes of the phenomenon. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sapphire-grown semiconductor film sets bandgap record
item.description: Semiconductors with wider bandgaps could pave the way for smaller, more efficient electronics that can handle far higher voltages, but the wider this gap becomes, the harder it is to control how well a material conducts electricity. Now, a team led by Darrell Schlom at Cornell University has shown that adding silicon to thin films of aluminum gallium oxide can keep this control intact at bandgaps wider than any semiconductor before it. Their research has been published in Nature. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Coffee calories have jumped nearly 40%. Sugar isn't the biggest culprit
item.description: Your morning coffee may be packing more calories than you realize, and sugar isn't the biggest reason. A study of 30,000 Americans found that non-dairy creamer has overtaken sugar and milk as the leading source of added coffee calories, helping drive a nearly 40% increase between 2003 and 2018. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Scientists discover a surprising secret behind the human brain’s wrinkles
item.description: Scientists have discovered why common marmosets have unusually small, smooth brains despite starting development much like other primates. The secret lies in subtle changes to brain-building cells that slow neuron production, revealing new clues about how the large, folded human brain evolved. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Algae-powered soft robot arm uses light to grasp and lift small objects
item.description: Tiny underwater algae sway gently in the current. All of a sudden, a light shines on them and they form robotlike arms that start to pick up small rocks and put them in floating baskets. Sounds like science fiction, but researchers from Delft University of Technology (the Netherlands) have created a small soft robot arm covered with minuscule algae that can grasp and lift objects. And it's powered by light. This next step in biotechnology has been published in Nature Communications. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: India capital steps up air pollution controls ahead of winter
item.description: India began annual measures on Thursday to tackle toxic air pollution in New Delhi, a megacity of 30 million people regularly ranked among the world's most polluted capitals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Big pharma accused of ‘free-riding on nature’ as global fund attracts just $7,000
item.description: The Cali Fund, set up to raise $1bn a year for biodiversity from drug companies, remains near empty Big pharmaceutical companies have been accused of “free-riding on nature”, after a landmark biodiversity fund that invites businesses to put some of their profits back into conservation was left virtually empty. The Cali Fund set out to raise $1bn (£750m) annually, by asking companies that profit from nature’s genetics to contribute towards conservation in low-income countries. But more than 18 months after the fund was launched, it remains far below this target. Continue reading... Publicado también por: The Guardian - Environment. Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Ratcliffe

item.title: ESA Open Days 2026
item.description: Video: 00:00:49 ESA Open Days 2026 welcomed over 23 000 visitors across its six establishments, giving the public the opportunity to discover more about Europe’s space activities, meet the people behind the missions and explore how ESA is shaping the future of space. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: ESA Council approves appointment of two new directors
item.description: The European Space Agency Council has approved the appointment of two new directors: Andrzej Banasiak as Director of Commercialisation and Industry Partnership, and Nicolaus Hanowski as Director of Space Operations. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.title: Proms, parties and gender politics: amazing photos from American dancefloors – and what they tell us about a changing nation
item.description: From George Balanchine to the Rockettes, the US magazine regularly ran lavish photo spreads dedicated to dance, with the myriad ways people moved their bodies holding up a mirror to the shifting times Life magazine launched in 1936. Its aim: to show the US the world, in pictures. At a time when television was still an experimental medium, a golden age of photojournalism brought the outside world into people’s homes. Life ran weekly until 1972, spanning a transformative time in US culture. Photographers were dispatched across the globe, covering wars, political manoeuvres, social trends… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.
item.dc:creator: Lyndsey Winship

item.title: China's Bohai Bay oyster reefs show recovery, with 286 oysters per square metre
item.description: A study of oyster reef restoration in China's Bohai Bay has found encouraging signs of marine habitat recovery between 2022 and 2026. By March 2026, artificial reefs supported an average of 286 oysters per square metre, while suspended particles in the water had declined by approximately 62%. Published in Frontiers in Marine Science, the study also recorded an increase in seabed animals. However, researchers said further monitoring was needed to establish the project's long-term effectiveness. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Colonizar Marte nos va a romper literalmente el corazón
item.description: La conquista de Marte es el próximo gran salto de la exploración espacial, pero el cuerpo humano no ha evolucionado lo suficiente para sobrevivir en el espacio profundo. Esto es un grave problema, puesto que nos exige tener tecnología puntera para enviar una tripulación al planeta rojo, pero también hay un cuello de botella biológico. El otro peligro. Históricamente, la principal preocupación médica ha sido el riesgo de cáncer por la exposición a la radiación cósmica. Sin embargo, un nuevo estudio financiado por la NASA ha puesto el foco en otro órgano vital como es el corazón. Esta… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Baby manta rays hunker down close to coasts before facing the open ocean's dangers
item.description: Giant manta rays can grow up to nine meters (30 feet) long with a disk size of seven meters (23 feet) across and weigh up to 2,000 kg (4,400 pounds). This size leaves them with very few natural enemies once they reach adulthood at around eight to 10 years old. But giant manta ray babies, called pups, cannot rely on their size to protect them from predators that live in the open ocean, including several species of shark and orcas. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: When powerful women are remembered as witches, we should challenge the historical motive
item.description: Reclaiming the label "witch" has become an act of feminist solidarity. But are we recovering the women themselves, or a posthumous identity built from accusation rather than fact? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Natural compound could fight rheumatoid arthritis at its source
item.description: A natural compound extracted from a medicinal plant has shown surprising promise against rheumatoid arthritis. In rats, it reduced joint swelling, protected cartilage, and calmed the immune responses responsible for chronic inflammation. Scientists discovered that the compound works by targeting a specific protein and restoring balance to fatty acid metabolism, revealing a previously underexplored way to fight the disease. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A simple 15-minute treatment could help patients avoid carpal tunnel surgery
item.description: A simple, steroid-free procedure could offer lasting relief for people struggling with carpal tunnel syndrome, potentially helping them avoid surgery. In a clinical trial involving 63 patients, researchers found that ultrasound-guided hydrodissection, which uses fluid to free a compressed nerve in the wrist, provided longer-lasting improvements in pain, numbness, and hand function than traditional steroid injections. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: SpaceX ya gana más con IA que con cohetes: el 52% de sus ingresos vienen de la IA
item.description: La división de IA en SpaceX, ahora rebautizada como “Super Intelligence”, ha sido la gran protagonista en los resultados financieros del último trimestre de la empresa. Y es que por primera vez, ha sido la división que más ingresos ha generado, por encima incluso de Starlink . Si bien Wall Street apuntaba alto en las previsiones, la compañía ha roto con todos los moldes. Récord . SpaceX ha registrado 14.600 millones de dólares en ingresos durante el Q3 de este año, un aumento del 161 % con respecto al año anterior. Su división de IA ingresó unos 7.600 millones de dólares, un 52% del total… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Vallejo

item.title: Illegal fishing is thriving in African waters—a satellite system could help change that
item.description: A patrol boat off the coast of Gabon intercepted three trawlers in July 2026, inside the Grand Sud Reserve. This is one of West and Central Africa's largest marine reserves, where industrial trawling is banned. None of the trawlers held a valid license. The patrol found them because analysts at the nonprofit Global Fishing Watch had studied satellite data and worked out where to look. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
item.description: Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates. The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: More young people are being recruited as 'money mules' by organized crime groups, new analysis reveals
item.description: More than 8,900 people aged under 30 were arrested for money laundering offenses in England and Wales between 2020 and 2025. That's more than six in 10 of all money laundering arrests recorded during the period. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Horror films exploit how human vision works to deliver movies' best scares
item.description: Imagine you're in the movie theater watching 2018's "Hereditary." During one of the film's most unsettling sequences, the main character, Peter, wakes up in bed disoriented. As he sits up, you hear a couple of gasps from others in the audience. The camera stays locked on Peter as he moves through his house and enters the dim living room. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Christina Koch, astronauta de Artemis II, de 47 años: “Para explorar el universo y otros planetas, primero debemos entender cómo cuidar el nuestro”
item.description: Luego de completar con éxito el histórico sobrevuelo lunar, se conoció una frase que pronunció mientras realizaba la misión; dejó de ser astronauta en activo tras ser nombrada recientemente como subeditora de ingeniería de la NASA Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Student motivation and responsibility shown to be key to tackling bullying in physical education
item.description: Physical education has traditionally been one of the most eagerly awaited classes of the school day, since it lets students get out of the classroom, move around and interact with their classmates in a different way—conditions that are conducive to learning values such as camaraderie and cooperation. However, the physical exposure and the dynamics of interaction, comparison and competition that the class can entail still make some students uneasy, and, in settings where bullying occurs, turn it into a potentially unsafe space. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Private business fortunes reveal overlooked source of wealth and inequality in America
item.description: A majority of Americans blame billionaires for the nation's ever-growing income and wealth divide. But economists Eric Zwick and Owen Zidar say there's a much larger but little-known cadre of very rich folks who may be even more important in closing the gap. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Four questions about schoolwork feedback to guide young students' learning
item.description: What happens when a young student gets a low math score? A parent may say, "Math has never been your strength." A teacher might write "careless" beside a calculation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Faster to Science: A Letter to the Science Community
item.description: NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Africans reuse, repair, recycle and resell waste: What's needed to build on the circular economy basics
item.description: In many African cities, a broken fridge is rarely thrown away immediately. It may be repaired and resold, dismantled for spare parts or collected for its metal components. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can a 'lullaby' save coral reefs from extinction?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03414-3 From underwater speakers to growing super-corals, scientists battle to save reefs around the world. Fuente: Nature.

item.description: Nature, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03389-1 As machines race ahead in solving problems, mathematicians must establish a new era that prizes human understanding over simply publishing more solutions. Fuente: Nature.

item.title: Venomous primate thought lost to science for nearly a century turns up in gardens and on roads across Indonesia
item.description: A big-eyed, venomous primate that had not been documented in scientific literature since the 1930s has been hiding in plain sight on the Indonesian island of Bangka, turning up in backyards, along roadsides and on power lines and prompting local residents who find them to call the Alobi Wildlife Rescue Center for help. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Holding out or holding back? Kindergarten redshirting and retention shifted sharply during the pandemic
item.description: By the time a child reaches the age of 4 or 5, most parents and caregivers have heard about "kindergarten readiness." But what if a 5-year-old still struggles to count to 10, sing the alphabet song or play cooperatively with other children? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New optogenetic tool inhibits activity in neurons and heart muscle cells
item.description: Researchers from Ruhr University Bochum have partnered with colleagues in Göttingen, Berlin, Paris and Essen to develop new optogenetic tools that can selectively inhibit cellular activity through light. These tools could help investigate diseases in which the balance between excitation and inhibition is disrupted, such as cardiac arrhythmias. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: U.K. exam board science specifications reveal gender gap that may influence girls' STEM choices
item.description: An absence of women scientists in U.K. exam board specifications for science could be a factor in the disproportionate number of girls dropping STEM subjects at 16 and contribute to the gender gap in STEM careers, new research from the University of Cambridge has found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Candida auris: A harbinger of further dangerous fungal species?
item.description: Why has the yeast Candida auris become a dangerous pathogen worldwide in just a few years? This question is on the minds of many researchers. Carla Schuh and Chaitanya Gokhale from the Biocentre at the University of Würzburg have now summarized the current state of knowledge in a review article in the journal mSphere. To that end, they analyzed around 180 studies by other researchers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Laser-made lattice reveals discrete light solitons in tunable atomic vapor
item.description: Scientists from the Quantum Technologies Group at the Institute of Physics Zagreb, in collaboration with a colleague from the Physics Department at the Faculty of Science (PMF), have experimentally demonstrated for the first time the existence of discrete one-dimensional (1D) solitons in an optically induced photonic lattice in warm rubidium vapor. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How rice coordinates signals to partner with beneficial soil fungi
item.description: Most plants do not gather nutrients from the soil entirely on their own. Many form partnerships with microscopic fungi that grow inside their roots and extend into the surrounding soil. These partnerships, known as arbuscular mycorrhizal symbioses, help plants access nutrients, especially phosphorus. In return, the fungi receive carbon-rich compounds from the plants. But how does a plant coordinate the many signals needed to build and maintain this exchange? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Perovskite laser maintains stable performance over 400 million pulses
item.description: In a study published in Advanced Optical Materials, researchers at Vilnius University (VU) demonstrated perovskite-based laser structures that maintained stable performance over more than 400 million pulses. Their findings address one of the major challenges limiting the practical use of perovskites: their instability. These semiconductor materials could play an important role in next-generation optical technologies, but their tendency to degrade has long posed a challenge for researchers worldwide. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Why the humble rabbit might be Australia's worst introduced species
item.description: The 19th-century pastoralist Thomas Austin was homesick. He yearned for the pastimes of his home in England—especially rabbit hunting. He asked his family to send him some rabbits. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Not all rattlesnakes are alike: Research suggests personality influences how rattlesnakes use their venom
item.description: Imagine encountering a rattlesnake in your backyard or while on a hike. It will most likely "freeze" to avoid attracting attention, but if it feels especially threatened, it may rattle and even strike, delivering a painful dose of venom. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Wild fish are a precious resource—here's how aquaculture can bolster food security
item.description: Small fish such as sardinella are an affordable source of protein and essential nutrients for millions of people across West Africa. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How a massive ice shelf buttressed the last ice age's glaciers—and what it could mean for Antarctica today
item.description: About 20,000 years ago, an enormous, floating ice shelf more than a mile (1.6 kilometers) thick helped lock in three of the largest ice sheets in northern Canada and Greenland. When that ice shelf disappeared, it helped unlock part of these ice sheets, which contributed to hundreds of feet of sea level rise, establishing modern coastlines as we know them. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Hearing laughter may cause orangutans to value rewards more
item.description: A new study from Indiana University shows that being in a positive mood leads orangutans to value what they learned more strongly. The study comes from the lab of Erica Cartmill, professor of animal behavior, anthropology and cognitive science in the College of Arts and Sciences at IU Bloomington, and was led by Daan Laméris, a postdoctoral researcher at IU. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: El Niño is threatening California's fragile coast again—the 1982–83 El Niño opened eyes to the serious erosion risks
item.description: California's coastal bluffs and beaches look rugged, but they can be surprisingly fragile in the face of a powerful El Niño. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Conducts RS-25 Engine Test in Support of Future Artemis Missions
item.description: NASA tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21 on the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. Test teams fired the developmental engine for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the same amount of time RS-25 engines fire during launch of NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket. During […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: LaToya Dean

item.title: Japan's expensive funerals and declining birthrates are transforming ancestral traditions
item.description: Whenever I drive amid the mazelike bustle of Tokyo's Shuto Expressway, where approximately 1 million vehicles transit daily, I see billboard advertisements for all manner of businesses: dentists, hotels, car and tire companies, and affordable funerals. Lots and lots of funerals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Salt marshes are proving to be powerful allies in building a climate-resilient coastline
item.description: Salt marsh sediment and vegetation can remain largely intact even during extreme storm surges. This was demonstrated in a large-scale experiment in which researchers transported sections of salt marsh to an experimental facility capable of producing the world's largest artificial waves. The results show how salt marshes can contribute to natural coastal protection, both in the Netherlands and beyond. The results were published in the journals Nature and Communications Sustainability. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Reconstructing 16,000 years of summer temperature change in the Western Balkans
item.description: Researchers at Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) have reconstructed approximately 16,000 years of summer temperature changes from sediments collected at Lake Prokoško in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The findings show how the Western Balkans responded to rapid climate changes at the end of the last glacial period, how warmer and cooler phases unfolded during the Holocene, and how the impact of human land use became increasingly pronounced. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI designs functional enzyme components that could help expand drug discovery
item.description: New active ingredients for drugs to treat infections, cancer or other serious diseases are often based on substances originally discovered in microorganisms, plants or other living organisms. Producing or improving such active ingredients in a targeted manner using microorganisms is often challenging because the underlying biological processes are extremely complex. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A scuff on your bag, a dent in your mug—and suddenly it feels like time for a new one
item.description: Imagine you have a bag you really like. It felt like "the one" when you bought it. Over time, it starts to look worn. There are some scuffs on it. Nothing is actually wrong with the bag, and it still works exactly as it should. Yet, once you notice those imperfections, you start thinking about buying a new one to replace it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Snail shell rings could hold prehistoric cyclone information
item.description: Snail growth could be linked to extreme weather rather than annual patterns, enabling researchers to determine past cyclones. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Nikki Sorbello and David Dowsett

item.title: Breaking through the 'fog of war': Game-based study suggests shared boundaries can foster peace
item.description: What causes adversaries to escalate conflicts into costly, prolonged wars even when neither side wants to fight? And in the fog of war, what might help them break that cycle and find a path to peace? Fuente: Phys.org.
